recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. Future changes to this boundary family should be handled as a new OO/PC workflow-boundary decision rather than as a remaining FHIR-17342 application gap.
issue_request: FHIR-17342 was Published with resolution Persuasive for STU3. It asked OO to review and clarify Task/Procedure/ServiceRequest/Encounter boundaries after Procedure scope broadened, distinguishing administrative workflow Tasks from clinical or physical activities and recognizing office visits as Encounter rather than Procedure.
initial_application: The Jira issue linked the implementers Zulip thread "Task vs Procedure Boundaries". Commit 5686ff744511d305f4c9602e3423018133e3fa6c (GF#17342) applied the seed by adding Boundaries and Relationships prose to active Task and ServiceRequest narrative source. That prose distinguished Task as spanning intent/event and tracking administrative workflow execution, Procedure as an event/activity resulting in change to or for the subject, and ServiceRequest as the request/authorization a Task may fulfill.
additional_context: The same boundary discussion continued through tightly related Published issues FHIR-17359 and FHIR-19109, which added and refined the Task/Procedure boundary text now present in Procedure and Task. Later Applied R6 issues FHIR-46344, FHIR-46341, and FHIR-47461 refined the same Task and ServiceRequest paragraphs with Request-pattern fulfillment and ServiceRequest authorization guidance; all of those related issue keys are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current fhir.ini lists Task, Procedure, ServiceRequest, and Encounter as active resources, and current narrative source covers Task workflow tracking, ServiceRequest request/authorization and fulfillment separation, Procedure actions that change the subject, and Encounter/Appointment/Procedure encounter boundaries.
